metadata.description: Standards bypass configuration for this branch

bypass.reason: An identity pin, not a reach: seat_email's owner lookup must BE guard.owner_address, one implementation of 'who owns this project' (the 2026-08-21 two-answers bug). No behaviour shows the difference until a second copy drifts.

route_command's bool is the module's claim on the command, not its verdict. A module that raised is reported by name through error(), which marks the command failed, so resolve_exit answers 2 and a chained next step does not run; the shell can tell. A re-raise would hand drone a traceback for a module defect, and False would exit 1 as 'unknown command', which it is not (pinned in tests/test_devpulse.py test_route_command_catches_module_errors).

CLI handler contract (fleet green, devpulse 2026-10-04; ai_mail leg 9 precedent). A _handle_* return is 'command recognised', not 'it worked': the router stops on True. Every line follows a cli error(), which marks the command failed and sets the non-zero exit, so the caller is told by that flag, never by the bool.

Fail closed. 53: a key file that exists but is not hex reads as no key, so nothing is signed or verified (logged as an error). 132: an unreadable caller passport answers '', which matches no seat, so the ceremony refuses. Neither can grant anything.

An unreadable CHANGELOG gives no headline, and compose_body then says so in the mail itself ('could not be read on the sending machine - open the release notes above'); the failure is logged as an error. The reader is told, not misled.

None is 'cannot read this passport', and its one caller (discover_managers) lists that path in skipped with reason 'passport unreadable - see the log', which the run reports. Never counted as a non-manager.

compass/ is the devpulse-owned Compass decision store (SQLite/FTS5 — db + wal + shm) which needs its own directory. Legitimate data subdir, not operator-config (custom_config/) nor auto-gen root data. Sanctioned exception per #643.

A lock primitive with no operation of its own to log; its callers (watch registry, feedback inbox) log the reads and writes it guards. Its one log_operation was the fcntl-absent (Windows) path, removed with Linux only (2026-11-14).

Watchdog presentation layer — console.print() IS the output. Same sanctioned shape as the feedback display handlers below: every function here renders a handler result dict for the operator and decides nothing. Split out of apps/modules/watchdog.py on 2026-08-22, which had reached 692 lines across r2/r3/r4 and broke the 600-line module ceiling; the display functions were the cohesive third that shared no state with the routing code.
Feedback handler — console.print() IS the output. Display functions are the handler's purpose.
Feedback handler — console.print() IS the output. Display functions are the handler's purpose.
format_wait() has 5 passing tests. Public utility for schedule display, not called in production yet.

A module that fails to import is skipped so the other verbs still run. Who finds out: the caller, on stderr, on every invocation (warning 'module X failed to load'), plus the ERROR line in devpulse's log that medic picks up.
A key that is not valid hex reads as no key: fails closed. Who finds out: the caller, whose admin action is refused with the reason, and the ERROR line in devpulse's log.
An unreadable caller passport reads as no caller: unverifiable means refused. Who finds out: the caller, refused at the gate, and the WARNING line in devpulse's log.
Status is a read-out: an unreadable cert shows as empty fields, and the same call runs verify_admin_grant and prints its failing leg. Who finds out: whoever ran status, on screen.
An unreadable CHANGELOG sends the release mail without its headline rather than no mail. Who finds out: medic, from the ERROR line; every manager sees a mail with no headline.
An unreadable stamp file reads as empty and flagged unreadable, never as already sent: a duplicate mail beats a silent release. Who finds out: medic, from the ERROR line; managers get the mail twice.
One unreadable passport must not stop the release mail to every other manager. Who finds out: devpulse, from the WARNING line naming the path; that one seat misses the mail.
None means unknown, not idle: the caller treats an unreadable transcript as in flight and never caches it, so the watch keeps running. Who finds out: the watcher, who sees the agent stay in flight.
A transcript line caught mid-write is skipped so the walk reaches the last line with a role. Who finds out: nobody needs to; the next poll reads the finished line.
An unparseable last rollout line is Codex mid-write and counts as in flight, the loud direction: the watch keeps running. Who finds out: the watcher, on the next poll.
A transcript rolled or cleaned between polls is dropped from the scan: deletion is not activity. Who finds out: the log line names the file; the watch goes on with the files that remain.

The strptime loops try the two timestamp formats mail writes; an unreadable sent file is skipped. A miss reads as no reply, the loud direction. Who finds out: the watcher, told completed_silent, CHECK DELIVERABLES.
A feed file that does not exist yet has no stat: None means nothing to drain. Who finds out: nobody needs to; the feed appears with the first event.
An unreadable feed drains nothing and keeps the cursor, so the same lines are tried again on the next tick. Who finds out: devpulse, from the WARNING line each tick.
No usable grounding receipt leaves the reading blank on the completion line; it is a display field, never a verdict. Who finds out: the reader, who sees no grounding shown.
None means /proc had no entry: not an answer about the state, and the caller treats it so. Who finds out: the liveness check that follows, which reports the pid gone.
Display only: a stamp that is not ISO is printed as it is. Who finds out: the reader, who sees the raw stamp.
None means the pid is gone or fd/1 unreadable: the target is unknown and callers treat unknown as not this wire. Who finds out: the dead-monitor check, which ends the wire with a report.
An empty cmdline means the process is gone; callers match on content, so empty matches nothing. Who finds out: the caller, which reports the pid as not a watchdog.
An unreadable dead-cursor reads as nothing announced, the loud direction: a DEAD dispatch is announced again. Who finds out: devpulse, woken twice, and the WARNING line.
Display only: a register stamp that is not ISO is shown verbatim. Who finds out: the reader, who sees the raw stamp.
With no sealed seat the reply hint drops its address; the CHECK DELIVERABLES line still prints. Who finds out: the reader, who sees the hint without an address.
